description: DNS rebinding attacks — exploit time-of-check-to-time-of-use on DNS resolution to pivot from an attacker-controlled domain to internal/localhost services. Detects susceptibility markers: missing Host header validation, no DNS pinning, browser-resolvable internal endpoints.

time_based_rebind.description: Classic TTL-based DNS rebinding: attacker DNS responds with external IP on first query, then 127.0.0.1 on second query after TTL expires. Tests whether the application re-resolves DNS mid-session and whether Host header validation prevents the pivot.

probes.description: DNS rebinding canary via Collaborator subdomain — if the application fetches this URL, the DNS lookup is observable; a second fetch after TTL expiry would resolve to a different IP

matchers.description: DNS or HTTP interaction confirms the app resolves and fetches attacker-controlled DNS

probes.description: Check response for absence of DNS pinning indicators — X-DNS-Prefetch-Control: off, strict Host validation, or IP-literal-only fetch patterns

matchers.name: X-DNS-Prefetch-Control
matchers.description: Missing DNS prefetch control header — browser may cache and reuse DNS across origins

host_header_rebind_susceptibility.description: Test whether the server validates the Host header against expected values. An app that accepts any Host header is susceptible to DNS rebinding — the attacker's domain resolves to the server's IP, and the request carries the attacker's Host.

probes.description: Send request with Host: evil.com to the target IP — 200 with normal content means the app does not validate Host, enabling DNS rebinding pivot
Send request with Host: 127.0.0.1 — if accepted, localhost services may be reachable via DNS rebinding to 127.0.0.1

websocket_rebind.description: WebSocket DNS rebinding — WebSocket connections are not bound by same-origin policy for established connections. If the server does not validate the Origin header on WS upgrade, an attacker page can open a WS to a rebinding domain that resolves to the target.

probes.description: WebSocket upgrade with Origin: http://evil.com — accepted upgrade without origin check enables cross-origin WS access via DNS rebinding
